title_en: Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. Coal Marketing and Distribution Department v. Shanxi Coking Coal Group International Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract
ruling_gist_en: In a closed-loop circular trading involving three or more enterprises, where one party sells and then buys back the same subject matter within the same period, selling low and buying high, which clearly contradicts the business purpose and commercial common sense of a for-profit legal person, such abnormal trading is in essence a lending relationship between enterprises disguised as a sale. The sale and purchase contracts entered into by the enterprises for this purpose constitute a sham expression of intent jointly implemented by the parties and shall be deemed invalid.

full_text_en:
[Case Name] Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. Coal Marketing and Distribution Department v. Shanxi Coking Coal Group International Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract

【Ruling Summary】

In a closed-loop circular transaction involving three or more enterprises, if one enterprise, within the same period, first sells and then purchases the same subject matter, selling at a low price and buying at a high price, such conduct clearly contradicts the business purpose and commercial common sense of a profit-making legal person. Such an abnormal transaction is in substance a loan relationship between enterprises concealed under the guise of a sale and purchase. The sales and purchase contracts entered into by the enterprises for this purpose constitute a false expression of intent jointly implemented by the parties and shall be deemed invalid.

In the actual loan relationship between the enterprises, the intermediary enterprise (the "pallet" enterprise) does not borrow funds for its own production or operational needs, but rather for the purpose of on-lending at a profit. Therefore, the loan contract shall also be deemed invalid. After the loan contract is invalid, the borrower shall return the principal and interest of the loan to the lender. If the lender also has fault in the invalidity of the contract, the people's court may appropriately reduce the amount of interest to be returned by the borrower.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Min Ti Zi No. 74

Reapplying Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. Address: Middle Section of Huanghai First Road, Rizhao City, Shandong Province.

Person in Charge: Zhu Tongxing, Manager of the Department.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Yao, lawyer of Shandong Luhai Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lyu Zuowu, employee of the Department.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shanxi Coking Coal Group International Development Co., Ltd. Address: 23rd Floor, Block A, Shanxi International Trade Center, No. 69 Fuxi Street, Taiyuan City, Shanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Zhu Chengjiang, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Huang Zhenguo, lawyer of Beijing Jingcheng Law Firm.

The reapplying applicant, Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Rizhao Port Marketing Department), in the case of a loan contract dispute with the respondent, Shanxi Coking Coal Group International Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shanxi Coking Coal Company), filed an application for retrial with this Court, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2014) Jin Shang Zhong Zi No. 7 rendered by the Shanxi High People's Court. Upon review, this Court issued a civil ruling (2014) Min Shen Zi No. 2090, deciding to bring the case for retrial, and formed a collegial panel composed of presiding judge Wang Fubo, acting judges Lin Haiquan and Zhang Ying to conduct the trial, with clerk Li Jie serving as the recorder. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The following facts were found through the trial of first instance by the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court, Shanxi Province:

On January 9, 2007, Shanxi Coking Coal Company, Rizhao Port Marketing Department, and a third party, Zhaoqing Xijiang Energy Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhaoqing Company), entered into a cooperation agreement, which stipulated: 1. Shanxi Coking Coal Company and Zhaoqing Company were responsible for purchasing coal and road transportation; Rizhao Port Marketing Department and Zhaoqing Company were responsible for port matters, and Zhaoqing Company was also responsible for coal sales and payment collection; 2. The coal price of Shanxi Coking Coal Company should not be higher than the port market price; if Shanxi Coking Coal Company could not dispatch the coal to the port as scheduled, it should refund the advance payment made by Rizhao Port Marketing Department within 15 days; 3. Separate contracts should be signed between the parties on a monthly basis according to coal quantity, price, and quality; 4. In principle, Rizhao Port Marketing Department should make advance payments to Shanxi Coking Coal Company for settlement, and Shanxi Coking Coal Company should make advance payments to Zhaoqing Company for settlement.

It was further found that on December 4, 2006, March 1, 2007, and April 23, 2007, Rizhao Port Marketing Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Company signed "Coal Purchase and Sales Contracts" at a coal price of RMB 523 per ton, with the loading port being Jingtang Port, Tangshan, and the delivery method being free on board (FOB) at the port of dispatch. After the contracts were signed, Rizhao Port Marketing Department paid RMB 7.6 million to Shanxi Coking Coal Company on June 29, 2007, and RMB 10 million on July 12, 2007, totaling RMB 17.6 million. However, Shanxi Coking Coal Company failed to supply the coal as agreed. On July 12, 2007, Shanxi Coking Coal Company issued a certificate stating: "We have received payment of RMB 17.6 million from the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. It is planned to load the vessel in mid-to-late July 2007. Upon negotiation, we will first issue a VAT invoice for the amount of RMB 20,050,564.80, which corresponds to 38,337.6 tons of Inner Mongolia raw coal for the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. We guarantee that this batch of coal will be transferred to the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. at the port before the end of July 2007." On July 1, 2009, Shanxi Coking Coal Company again issued a certificate stating: "We have received a transaction payment of RMB 17.6 million from the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. (originally planned for vessel loading in mid-to-late July 2007). 38,337.6 tons of Inner Mongolia raw coal have not been delivered to the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. We guarantee that this batch of coal will be transferred to the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. at Rizhao Port before the end of July 2009." Subsequently, Shanxi Coking Coal Company again failed to supply the coal as agreed.

It was further found that Shanxi Coking Coal Company and Zhaoqing Company signed coal purchase and sales contracts on December 4, 2006, January 22, 2007, and April 23, 2007, at a price of RMB 510 per ton. The loading port was Jingtang Port, Tangshan, and the delivery method was FOB at the port of dispatch. Zhaoqing Company failed to dispatch the coal as agreed. Shanxi Coking Coal Company stated that it had requested Zhaoqing Company to deliver the coal to Rizhao Port Marketing Department, and if delivery could not be made, to refund the RMB 17.6 million to Rizhao Port Marketing Department, but Shanxi Coking Coal Company did not provide evidence to support its claim.

Because Zhaoqing Company did not appear in court for questioning, Rizhao Port Marketing Department did not provide its purchase and sales contract with Zhaoqing Company to the court. However, the two parties had business dealings in 2007. Rizhao Port Marketing Department delivered 80,836.2 tons of coal to Zhaoqing Company at a price of RMB 533 per ton, with a total receivable payment of RMB 43,085,598.66. From April 2, 2007, to July 25, 2007, Rizhao Port Marketing Department actually received RMB 43.4 million, with an overpayment of RMB 314,401.34. The RMB 17.6 million was only part of the payment. On September 30, 2007, Zhaoqing Company paid freight of RMB 350,000. On October 29, 2009, Rizhao Port Marketing Department settled accounts with Zhaoqing Company, and Rizhao Port Marketing Department paid Zhaoqing Company RMB 248,226. There were no further business dealings between the parties thereafter.

Due to disputes arising from the performance of the contracts, Rizhao Port Marketing Department filed a lawsuit, requesting a judgment ordering Shanxi Coking Coal Company to deliver 38,337.6 tons of Inner Mongolia raw coal to Rizhao Port Marketing Department, or to refund the payment of RMB 17.6 million to Rizhao Port Marketing Department, and to compensate for corresponding interest losses (calculated from August 1, 2007, to the date of filing the lawsuit, amounting to RMB 4,106,108).

The court of first instance held that after Rizhao Port Marketing Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Company signed the coal purchase and sales contract, Rizhao Port Marketing Department paid an advance payment of RMB 17.6 million as agreed, but Shanxi Coking Coal Company did not deliver the goods as agreed. Moreover, on July 12, 2007, Shanxi Coking Coal Company issued a certificate stating: "We have received payment of RMB 17.6 million from the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. It is planned to load the vessel in mid-to-late July 2007. Upon negotiation, we will first issue a VAT invoice for the amount of RMB 20,050,564.80, which corresponds to 38,337.6 tons of Inner Mongolia raw coal for the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. We guarantee that this batch of coal will be transferred to the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. at the port before the end of July 2007." After January 2008, no cooperation agreement was signed among Shanxi Coking Coal Company, Rizhao Port Marketing Department, and Zhaoqing Company, nor were any coal purchase and sales contracts signed between any two of them. However, on July 1, 2009, Shanxi Coking Coal Company again issued a certificate stating: "We have received a transaction payment of RMB 17.6 million from the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. (originally planned for vessel loading in mid-to-late July 2007). 38,337.6 tons of Inner Mongolia raw coal have not been delivered to the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. We guarantee that this batch of coal will be transferred to the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port Group Co., Ltd. at Rizhao Port before the end of July 2009." However, Shanxi Coking Coal Company has not supplied the goods as agreed to date. Therefore, the facts that Shanxi Coking Coal Company received the payment but failed to deliver the goods are clear and supported by solid evidence. Shanxi Coking Coal Company should deliver 38,337.6 tons of Inner Mongolia raw coal to Rizhao Port Marketing Department, or refund the advance payment of RMB 17.6 million and pay corresponding interest. Shanxi Coking Coal Company claimed that the RMB 17.6 million it received from Rizhao Port Marketing Department had been refunded to Rizhao Port Marketing Department through Zhaoqing Company, but it failed to provide reliable and sufficient evidence to support this claim. The court did not sustain this defense. Accordingly, the court of first instance rendered civil judgment (2012) Bing Shang Chu Zi No. 119, ordering: 1. Shanxi Coking Coal Company shall deliver 38,337.6 tons of Inner Mongolia raw coal to Rizhao Port Marketing Department within ten days after the judgment takes effect. 2. If Shanxi Coking Coal Company fails to perform the obligation under item 1, it shall, within thirty days after the judgment takes effect, refund the principal payment of RMB 17.6 million to Rizhao Port Marketing Department together with interest (calculated from July 2, 2009, at the corresponding loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period until the date determined for performance). The court acceptance fee of RMB 150,331 shall be borne by Shanxi Coking Coal Company.

Shanxi Coking Coal Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Shanxi High People's Court, requesting the revocation of the civil judgment (2012) Bing Shang Chu Zi No. 119 of the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court, the dismissal of all claims of the appellee, and that the litigation costs be borne by the appellee.

The facts found by the court of second instance were consistent with those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that the issue in dispute was whether the RMB 17.6 million transferred by Zhaoqing Company to Rizhao Port Marketing Department was a refund of the advance payment made by Zhaoqing Company on behalf of Shanxi Coking Coal Company to Rizhao Port Marketing Department, or was a payment of the purchase price by Zhaoqing Company to Rizhao Port Marketing Department. On January 9, 2007, the three parties signed a cooperation agreement stipulating that, to protect the economic interests of each party, the costs in each link of coal marketing and transportation should be open and transparent and promptly communicated among the parties. The agreement further stipulated that the contracts signed between Rizhao Port Marketing Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Company, between Rizhao Port Marketing Department and Zhaoqing Company, and between Zhaoqing Company and Shanxi Coking Coal Company were all integral parts of this agreement. Therefore, the economic conduct between any two of the three parties should be carried out in accordance with the operational framework set forth in the three-party agreement and should be corroborated by corresponding coal purchase and sales contracts. If Rizhao Port Marketing Department claimed that the RMB 17.6 million transferred back by Zhaoqing Company was a payment for purchase price due from Zhaoqing Company, it should have provided the coal purchase and sales contract with Zhaoqing Company as evidence. Because Rizhao Port Marketing Department was unable to provide the contract, the court did not sustain Rizhao Port Marketing Department's argument that the RMB 17.6 million was a payment for the purchase price due from Zhaoqing Company. The court held that after the RMB 17.6 million in dispute had flowed sequentially among Rizhao Port Marketing Department, Shanxi Coking Coal Company, and Zhaoqing Company, the creditor-debt relationship among the three parties arising from this sum was extinguished. The appeal grounds of Shanxi Coking Coal Company were sufficient and should be sustained. The judgment of the court of first instance applied the law incorrectly and should be corrected. Pursuant to Item (2) of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court of second instance rendered civil judgment (2014) Jin Shang Zhong Zi No. 7, deciding to revoke the judgment (2012) Bing Shang Chu Zi No. 119 of the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court, and to dismiss all claims of Rizhao Port Marketing Department. The litigation costs for the first and second instances, each amounting to RMB 150,331, were to be borne by Rizhao Port Marketing Department.

Rizhao Port Marketing Department, dissatisfied with the judgment of second instance, filed an application for retrial with this Court, requesting that the judgment be reversed and the civil judgment (2012) Bing Shang Chu Zi No. 119 of the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court be upheld. The reasons for its application for retrial are:

1. The facts found in the judgment of second instance lacked evidentiary support. The basic facts of this case are:
(1) Since 2006, Rizhao Port Marketing Department had been engaging in coal trading business cooperation with Shanxi Coking Coal Company and Zhaoqing Company. The mode of cooperation was that Rizhao Port Marketing Department would make advance payments to purchase coal from Shanxi Coking Coal Company, load the coal at Jingtang Port, transport it to Guangdong, and then resell it to Zhaoqing Company. Zhaoqing Company would pay the full purchase price to Rizhao Port Marketing Department before taking delivery of the goods at the destination port. For each transaction, Rizhao Port Marketing Department would sign separate purchase and sales contracts with Shanxi Coking Coal Company and Zhaoqing Company, respectively, and conduct business operations in accordance with the terms of each contract.
(2) On December 4, 2006, and March 1, 2007, Rizhao Port Marketing Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Company signed "Coal Purchase and Sales Contracts" respectively. Rizhao Port Marketing Department purchased coal from Shanxi Coking Coal Company, and then resold the coal to Zhaoqing Company at a markup of RMB 10 per ton. Zhaoqing Company chartered the vessels "Yin Dong" and "Yin Bao" to transport the coal to Xinsha Port in Guangzhou for discharge. Rizhao Port Marketing Department actually sold a total of 80,836.02 tons of coal to Zhaoqing Company under these two shipments. By July 2007, Zhaoqing Company had paid the full purchase price (the last two payments being a telegraphic transfer of RMB 10 million on July 19, 2007, and a bank acceptance payment of RMB 7.6 million on July 25). Rizhao Port Marketing Department had also issued all VAT invoices and delivered all the goods. Thereafter, no new business transactions occurred between Rizhao Port Marketing Department and Zhaoqing Company until October 29, 2009, when they settled the outstanding balances from all prior transactions (Rizhao Port Marketing Department refunded Zhaoqing Company RMB 248,226.95).
(3) On April 23, 2007, Shanxi Coking Coal Company and Rizhao Port Marketing Department again signed a "Coal Purchase and Sales Contract" numbered "MNKX-2007-005". Rizhao Port Marketing Department made advance payments totaling RMB 17.6 million to Shanxi Coking Coal Company in two installments. However, this contract was not ultimately performed. At the request of Rizhao Port Marketing Department, the parties signed a supplementary "Coal Purchase and Sales Contract" numbered "MNKX-2007-005 Supplement" on July 12, 2007, changing the delivery time to the end of July 2007. On the same day, Shanxi Coking Coal Company issued a "Certificate" to Rizhao Port Marketing Department, confirming the fact that it had issued an invoice in advance but had not delivered the goods, and that it had received the advance payment of RMB 17.6 million, and undertaking to deliver the goods by the end of July 2007. However, Shanxi Coking Coal Company violated the agreement by failing to deliver the goods and also failed to refund the advance payment. On July 1, 2009, Shanxi Coking Coal Company again issued a "Certificate" to Rizhao Port Marketing Department. First, a fax copy was sent. After Rizhao Port Marketing Department received the fax, it requested the original document from Shanxi Coking Coal Company. However, the original document subsequently received from Shanxi Coking Coal Company had deleted the sentence: "We guarantee that this batch of coal will be transferred to the Coal Marketing and Distribution Department of Rizhao Port (Group) Co., Ltd. at Rizhao Port before the end of July 2009." Because Shanxi Coking Coal Company still failed to fulfill its commitment to deliver the coal and also failed to refund the advance payment, Rizhao Port Marketing Department filed this lawsuit with the court.

2. Rizhao Port Marketing Department had moved twice after 2007, and some business documents were unfortunately lost and have not been found to date, including the business contract with Zhaoqing Company involved in this case and some business contracts with Shanxi Coking Coal Company. However, to prove the existence and actual performance of a sales contract between Rizhao Port Marketing Department and Zhaoqing Company, Rizhao Port Marketing Department provided a large amount of evidence, including relevant VAT special invoices, bank vouchers, cargo delivery receipts, financial ledgers, and business archive materials obtained from the Guangzhou Xinsha Port authority. These documents, together with the financial materials of Zhaoqing Company obtained by the Taiyuan Intermediate Court from the Economic Investigation Detachment of the Zhaoqing City Public Security Bureau, mutually corroborate and are sufficient to prove that the RMB 17.6 million paid by Zhaoqing Company was payment for the purchase price. Considering the sales contract and supplementary agreement between Shanxi Coking Coal Company and Zhaoqing Company submitted by Shanxi Coking Coal Company to the court, the relationship between those two parties was not a simple purchase and sale relationship, but rather that Shanxi Coking Coal Company had entrusted or even lent money to Zhaoqing Company to purchase coal on its behalf, which was then sold to Rizhao Port Marketing Department and other customers (not every transaction involved Rizhao Port Marketing Department). The RMB 17.6 million paid by Shanxi Coking Coal Company to Zhaoqing Company was a matter between those two companies and had no relationship with Rizhao Port Marketing Department whatsoever.

3. The RMB 17.6 million paid by Rizhao Port Marketing Department to Shanxi Coking Coal Company was the advance payment under the supplementary sales contract numbered "MNKX-2007-005 Supplement" signed by the two parties on July 12, 2007. In contrast, the RMB 17.6 million paid by Zhaoqing Company to Rizhao Port Marketing Department was the purchase price for the coal shipped on the vessels "Yin Dong" and "Yin Bao". These two sums are completely different. Shanxi Coking Coal Company attempted to take advantage of the coincidence in the flow and amount of funds to avoid its repayment obligation. This argument is not only inconsistent with the objective facts and illogical, but also contradicts the existing evidence, and is therefore untenable.

4. The RMB 17.6 million was payment for the purchase price from Zhaoqing Company to Rizhao Port Marketing Department, not a refund of the advance payment made on behalf of Shanxi Coking Coal Company. The two "Certificates" issued by Shanxi Coking Coal Company to Rizhao Port Marketing Department on July 12, 2007, and July 1, 2009, directly prove that Shanxi Coking Coal Company received the advance payment but did not deliver the goods nor refund the money.

5. The judgment of second instance in this case was based solely on procedural law for altering the judgment, and no substantive law was applied to the determination of substantive issues, constituting an error in the application of law.

Shanxi Coking Coal Company argued in its defense: 1. The advance payment of RMB 17.6 million that Shanxi Coking Coal Company received from the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department had already been returned to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department through Zhaoqing Company. The "Tripartite Cooperation Agreement" is an important foundational document for determining the nature of this RMB 17.6 million. Shanxi Coking Coal Company's statement that the RMB 17.6 million had been returned to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department is consistent with the facts and evidence of this case and is reasonable. 2. The Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department's argument that the RMB 17.6 million was payment by Zhaoqing Company for the purchase of the two shiploads of cargo, "Yindong" and "Yinbao," is inconsistent with the factual evidence and contradicts common sense and logic, and is therefore legally unsustainable. The relevant financial accounts provided by the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department were all unilaterally prepared by them and provided in fragments, and cannot prove the actual transactions and fund flows between them and Zhaoqing Company. Their relevant calculations and results are not credible and lack probative value. Moreover, the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department has tampered with evidence, and should bear adverse consequences in accordance with law. In summary, Shanxi Coking Coal Company requests that the court reject the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department's claims in accordance with law and uphold the civil judgment (2014) Jin Shang Zhong Zi No. 7 of the Shanxi High People's Court. During the retrial of this court, Shanxi Coking Coal Company provided an "Explanation Concerning the RMB 17.6 Million Coal Cooperation Dispute Among Shanxi Coking Coal Group International Development Co., Ltd., the Rizhao Port Group Coal Transportation and Sales Department, and Zhaoqing Xijiang Energy Development Co., Ltd." issued by Zhaoqing Company to the Shanxi High People's Court on May 7, 2014, as well as an "Investigation Record" formed from an inquiry by Shanxi Coking Coal Company's attorney, Qiao Ligang, with Liang Shaofeng, the coal department manager of Zhaoqing Company, to prove that Zhaoqing Company had already returned the RMB 17.6 million advance payment to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department as instructed by Shanxi Coking Coal Company. The Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department challenged the evidence, arguing that this evidence does not constitute new evidence. The court of second instance had already received the above evidence mailed by a non-party during the second instance proceedings and had presented it to them, but did not organize both parties to examine it. Because the source of the evidence is unclear, the provider is not legally qualified, the authenticity of the official seal is uncertain, the veracity cannot be verified, and the content is false, it should not be used as a basis for determining the facts of the case. This court is of the opinion that both pieces of evidence above constitute witness testimony and do not constitute new evidence. The "Explanation" provided by Zhaoqing Company lacks the signature or seal of the unit's responsible person or the person who prepared it. In another related case being heard concurrently with this case, Zhaoqing Company, as a party, did not participate in the litigation from the first instance onward, and the people's court was unable to contact it. Relevant litigation documents were all served by public announcement. As for the other witness, Liang Shaofeng, Shanxi Coking Coal Company stated that it is now unable to contact him. Therefore, the source and authenticity of the above evidence cannot be verified, and the content of the evidence does not match the financial vouchers and fund transfer vouchers of Zhaoqing Company at the time of the transaction. Accordingly, this court does not recognize its probative value.

In addition to confirming the facts found by the original courts of first and second instance, this court further finds:

1. On December 4, 2006, the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department (buyer) and Shanxi Coking Coal Company (seller) signed a "Coal Purchase and Sale Contract," stipulating: "I. Subject matter, quantity: raw lump coal, 6,000 tons (\(\pm\)10%); II. Quality indicators...; III. Delivery time: December 2006, subject to vessel arrival at port; IV. Price: one-invoice tax-included Jingtang Port ex-factory price of RMB 523 per ton; V. Port of shipment: Tangshan Jingtang Port; VI. Method of delivery: delivered free on board at the port of shipment; VII. Quality standards: subject to inspection by the Jingtang Port Commodity Inspection Center; VIII. Quantity acceptance: subject to the port and shipping cargo handover list; IX. Payment and settlement: before loading, the buyer shall pay the full amount of the purchase price to the seller..." On the same day, Shanxi Coking Coal Company (buyer) and Zhaoqing Company (seller) also signed a "Coal Purchase and Sale Contract." The subject matter, quantity, quality indicators, delivery time, port of shipment, method of delivery, quality standards, and quantity acceptance of this contract were identical to those in the aforementioned contract, but the price was RMB 510 per ton.

2. On January 9, 2007, Shanxi Coking Coal Company, the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, and Zhaoqing Company signed a "Tripartite Cooperation Agreement," stipulating that the three parties would cooperate in the operation of 1 million tons of coal in 2007.

3. On July 19, 2007, Zhaoqing Company made an electronic transfer of RMB 10 million to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, with the purpose of remittance stated as "purchase price." The corresponding entry in Zhaoqing Company's financial accounting voucher No. 16 dated July 31, 2007, recorded: "Payment to Rizhao Port Group for purchase price RMB 10 million"; financial accounting voucher No. 39 recorded: "Endorsement payment to Rizhao Port Group for purchase price RMB 7.6 million."

4. In the related case (2011) Bing Shang Chu Zi No. 71 heard by the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court, Shanxi Coking Coal Company alleged: "The three parties essentially engaged in a circular flow of funds without any real transactional relationship." During the second instance of this case, Shanxi Coking Coal Company explained the transaction at issue: "Why did a closed chain form? The Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department bought coal from us, we bought coal from Zhaoqing Company, and then Zhaoqing Company bought coal from the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department. This was because Zhaoqing Company lacked funds. In reality, the coal was Zhaoqing Company's own, and Zhaoqing Company organized this whole matter."

This court is of the opinion that the focus of the dispute among the parties during the retrial is whether the RMB 17.6 million paid by Zhaoqing Company to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department was an advance payment returned to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department on behalf of Shanxi Coking Coal Company, and whether Shanxi Coking Coal Company is obligated to continue performing the coal purchase and sale contract or to return the advance payment and interest. Resolving this focal issue involves both factual determination regarding the tripartite transaction and payment situation, and a judgment on the nature and validity of the legal relationships among the three parties. This court makes the following analysis and determination:

I. Regarding whether the RMB 17.6 million paid by Zhaoqing Company to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department was an advance payment returned by Zhaoqing Company to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department on behalf of Shanxi Coking Coal Company. This court is of the opinion that, based on the existing evidence, it cannot be determined that the RMB 17.6 million paid by Zhaoqing Company to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department was an advance payment returned by Zhaoqing Company on behalf of Shanxi Coking Coal Company. Shanxi Coking Coal Company's claim that the RMB 17.6 million claim and debt between it and the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department has been extinguished is untenable. The reasons are:

First, Shanxi Coking Coal Company confirmed that the RMB 17.6 million debt between it and the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department had not been fully performed. Although Shanxi Coking Coal Company argued in the litigation that it had already returned the RMB 17.6 million to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department through two payments made by Zhaoqing Company in July 2007, and that the claims and debts between the parties had been extinguished, it failed to provide proof of instructing Zhaoqing Company to make the repayment, and it never notified the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department of the fact that it had instructed Zhaoqing Company to repay. On the contrary, nearly two years after Zhaoqing Company had paid the RMB 17.6 million to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, on July 1, 2009, Shanxi Coking Coal Company still issued a written certificate to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, confirming that the RMB 17.6 million raw coal sale debt between the parties had not been fully performed. Therefore, Shanxi Coking Coal Company's claim in the litigation contradicts the written certificate it issued before the litigation and is difficult to accept.

Second, the existing evidence can prove that Zhaoqing Company paid the RMB 17.6 million to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department as a purchase price owed by Zhaoqing Company to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, not as an advance payment returned on behalf of Shanxi Coking Coal Company. The courts of first and second instance had already found that there were business dealings between the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department and Zhaoqing Company in 2007. The Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department delivered 80,836.2 tons of goods to Zhaoqing Company, with receivables of RMB 43,085,598.66. From April 2, 2007, to July 25, 2007, the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department actually received RMB 43.4 million in payments. On the remittance voucher for the RMB 10 million transferred by Zhaoqing Company to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, the purpose of the remittance was clearly stated as "purchase price," not as a return of advance payment on behalf of Shanxi Coking Coal Company. In Zhaoqing Company's financial accounting vouchers, the remaining RMB 7.6 million was also recorded as "endorsement payment for purchase price" to Rizhao Port Group. When Zhaoqing Company and the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department settled their business accounts on October 29, 2009, this RMB 17.6 million was also settled as a purchase price paid by Zhaoqing Company to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department.

Third, the court of second instance's reason for denying that the RMB 17.6 million paid by Zhaoqing Company was a due purchase price is untenable. The court of second instance held that if the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department claimed that the RMB 17.6 million transferred back by Zhaoqing Company was a due purchase price payable by Zhaoqing Company, it should provide a coal purchase and sale contract with Zhaoqing Company to prove it. Because the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department could not provide the contract, the court of second instance did not support the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department's argument that the RMB 17.6 million was a due purchase price payable by Zhaoqing Company. However, in the section on found facts, the court of second instance had already confirmed that there were business dealings between the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department and Zhaoqing Company in 2007, that the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department delivered 80,836.2 tons of goods to Zhaoqing Company, with receivables of RMB 43,085,598.66, and that from April 2, 2007, to July 25, 2007, it actually received RMB 43.4 million in payments, of which the RMB 17.6 million was only part. On the one hand, the court of second instance recognized that there was a coal purchase and sale business relationship between the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department and Zhaoqing Company, and that the RMB 17.6 million paid was purchase price. On the other hand, it denied that the RMB 17.6 million paid by Zhaoqing Company was purchase price, on the ground that the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department failed to provide a coal purchase and sale contract with Zhaoqing Company. This is internally contradictory, and the reasoning of the judgment is clearly improper.

II. Regarding the nature of the legal relationship in this case and the validity of the contracts. On December 4, 2006, the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Company, and Shanxi Coking Coal Company and Zhaoqing Company, respectively signed "Coal Purchase and Sale Contracts" that were identical in subject matter, quantity, quality indicators, delivery time, port of shipment, method of delivery, quality standards, and quantity acceptance, except for the price. Zhaoqing Company, as the ultimate supplier, effectively obtained payment from the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department indirectly through the medium of Shanxi Coking Coal Company in the form of selling coal, and Shanxi Coking Coal Company obtained a price difference income of RMB 13 per ton. According to the facts that have been found, during the same period, the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department also signed a sales contract with Zhaoqing Company to resell the purchased coal to Zhaoqing Company at a price of RMB 533 per ton, thereby obtaining a price difference income of RMB 10 per ton. Through the above three transactions, the three parties, the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, Shanxi Coking Coal Company, and Zhaoqing Company, formed a closed-loop circular purchase and sale with an identical subject matter. Zhaoqing Company first sold coal at a low price of RMB 510 per ton to obtain payment, and after a certain period, bought coal at a high price of RMB 533 per ton and paid the price. In this circular sale, Zhaoqing Company was both seller and buyer, selling low and buying high, with a net loss of RMB 23 per ton. Zhaoqing Company knew that it would inevitably suffer losses in such a circular sale, and the more transactions, the greater the losses. Yet it still agreed with the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Company to cooperate in the operation of 1 million tons of coal in 2007. This is clearly inconsistent with Zhaoqing Company's status as a for-profit legal person, violates commercial common sense, and is sufficient to raise reasonable doubts about the authenticity of Zhaoqing Company's purchase and sale activities. In this regard, Shanxi Coking Coal Company explained that it was because Zhaoqing Company lacked funds that it organized such transactions on its own. Through a comprehensive examination of the transaction process in this case and analysis of the relevant evidence, this court is of the opinion that the relationships among the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, Shanxi Coking Coal Company, and Zhaoqing Company were not genuine coal purchase and sale relationships, but rather financing and lending activities in the form of coal purchase and sale. Zhaoqing Company, as the actual borrower, effectively paid a purchase price difference of RMB 23 per ton as interest. Only in this way can the reason why Zhaoqing Company both sold and bought, sold low and bought high, and willingly suffered losses be reasonably explained. Therefore, the nature of the legal relationship in this case should be inter-enterprise lending disguised as a purchase and sale. Accordingly, the cause of action in this case should also be a dispute over an inter-enterprise loan contract. The original courts of first and second instance improperly determined the cause of action to be a dispute over a sales contract, and this court corrects that determination. Because the "Coal Purchase and Sale Contracts" signed among the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, Shanxi Coking Coal Company, and Zhaoqing Company all lacked a genuine intention to buy and sell, and constituted a pretense of intention jointly made by the parties, they should all be deemed invalid.

Shanxi Coking Coal Company, the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, and Zhaoqing Company signed a "Tripartite Cooperation Agreement" on January 9, 2007, stipulating that the three parties would cooperate in the operation of 1 million tons of coal in 2007. It can be seen that the three parties had reached a consensus on carrying out inter-enterprise lending business in the form of coal purchase and sale on a long-term and repeated basis. The transaction involving RMB 17.6 million in this case was a specific performance of the tripartite agreement. The Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department does not have the qualifications to engage in financial business, yet it engaged in lending as a regular business and actually operated financial business, which violates relevant financial laws, regulations, and judicial policies. Shanxi Coking Coal Company borrowed from the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department in the form of a purchase and sale, not for production or operational needs, but to relend to Zhaoqing Company for profit. Therefore, the loan contracts actually formed in the form of purchase and sale between the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Company, and between Shanxi Coking Coal Company and Zhaoqing Company, should all be deemed invalid. According to the provisions of Article 58 of the Contract Law, after the loan contract between the parties in this case, the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Company, is invalidated, Shanxi Coking Coal Company shall return the RMB 17.6 million obtained from the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department, together with interest, to the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department. Because the Rizhao Port Coal Transportation and Sales Department also has fault for the invalidity of the lending act, the amount of interest to be returned by Shanxi Coking Coal Company may be appropriately reduced. This court, in accordance with the principle of fairness, determines that the amount of interest to be returned by Shanxi Coking Coal Company shall be calculated at the benchmark interest rate for deposits of the same type and same period published by the People's Bank of China. The dispute between Shanxi Coking Coal Company and the non-party Zhaoqing Company may be resolved in a separate action.

In summary, this court is of the opinion that the original judgments of first and second instance contained errors in fact finding and application of law, and this court corrects them. Pursuant to Article 11, Paragraph 2 of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 19 of the Banking Supervision and Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Item 2 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (2014) Jin Shang Zhong Zi No. 7 of the Shanxi High People's Court and the civil judgment (2012) Bing Shang Chu Zi No. 119 of the Taiyuan Intermediate People's Court are vacated;

2. The "Coal Purchase and Sale Contract" signed between the Rizhao Port Group Coal Transportation and Sales Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Group International Development Co., Ltd. is invalid;

3. Shanxi Coking Coal Group International Development Co., Ltd. shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, return RMB 17.6 million to the Rizhao Port Group Coal Transportation and Sales Department and pay interest (interest shall be calculated at the benchmark interest rate for deposits of the same type and same period published by the People's Bank of China, from August 1, 2007, until the actual date of payment within the period specified for performance in this judgment).

If the paying party fails to perform the payment obligation within the period specified in this judgment, it shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, double the interest for delayed performance from the date of delay.

The litigation costs for the first and second instances, each RMB 150,331, shall be borne equally by the Rizhao Port Group Coal Transportation and Sales Department and Shanxi Coking Coal Group International Development Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
